source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Here's an update: I've made some good progress today, and worked out a tentative breakdown that gets as far as Tom meeting Apollonia on comic page 12. I may end up deciding that pace is too brisk, if certain beats need more space to breathe--it's something I'll need to figure out as I go.
I have two questions, or rather two thoughts on how to approach the script that I want to check with you:
1.. In a few places I think I want to adapt parts of the scene descriptions into "voice over" caption text.
2\. There are a few short exchanges that I might want to omit for the sake of efficiency and page space. For example, at the bottom of page 23 where Carter tells Tom he's invited to the dinner he attends in the following scene.
I wanted to check whether deviations from the script of that size would be acceptable, or if you want the comic to represent the screenplay line-for-line. Let me know what you think.
Thanks.

ambiguity.description: It is unresolved whether the sample must follow the screenplay line-for-line or may use voice-over captions and omit minor exchanges for pacing.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
In that case, thank you very much. For that rate I will be able to spend some more time on the best way to present everything, rather than relying so closely on the screenplay.

Would you like me to get started on this next week, or should I wait for you to say "go?"

I can commit to scripting 80-85 comic pages. I'll look over the next two episodes and the novel, and work out how much of the story to cover in that space. As I do that, should I pace things with an eye toward eventually scripting the rest of the story? That is, should I aim for something that feels self-contained, or focus on leaving the reader asking, "What's next?"

Thanks,
Cory
